title: Pollinator decline and crop pollination
bottleneck: Roughly a third of crop production depends on animal pollinators, yet wild pollinator populations are declining from habitat loss, pesticides, and disease — and managed honeybees face colony-collapse pressures. There's no substitute for pollination at scale: hand-pollination works for vanilla, not for almonds. The decline is diffuse and hard to attribute, so coordinated action stalls while the losses compound. why_it_blocks: Pollinator-dependent crops include most fruits, vegetables, and nuts — the nutritious part of the diet. Their loss would collapse dietary diversity.
current_state: Habitat strips and reduced pesticide use help locally; global pollinator trends remain negative. A Harvard-led study links pollinator decline to 427,000 early deaths yearly from lost fruit and vegetable consumption.
